messages:
maria-support: FYI ACME just opened a ticket — embeddings vectors/sec dropped ~6x after last week's model-rollout. Tokens/sec looks normal. Customer seeing 200ms token latency but only ~10 vectors/sec per pod.

aj-eng: Can you paste the request sample + model id? is this only for their larger batch job or all calls?

maria-support: They provided a small repro payload and say it's on model-rex-3b-quant (pinned). Example request: ```POST /v1/embeddings { model: "rex-3b-quant", input: ["search term"], batch_size: 128 }``` They said batches that used to get ~1200 vecs/sec now ~180.

kevin-ml: Noted. Does the payload include any dimension override or legacy param? Any 0-length vectors returned?

maria-support: No dimension override. Their client logs show successful 200s but server logs have occasional: `WARN: embedding_dim_mismatch detected for client_id=acme-corp` — not sure what that means.

lina-frontend: Also saw a sudden spike in 429s from the auth gateway for that org around the same time window. billing-bot: [automated] billing throttle applied to acme-corp for suspected over-quota - window: 2026-03-15T10:02:00Z.

aj-eng: Hmm. Two streams: (A) auth/billing-induced retries changing request arrival pattern; (B) an embedding path regression (dim check or kvcache). Retries could lead to tiny microbursts that trip batching heuristics and GPU queue depth.

maria-support: Customer insists they did not change client code. They throttled themselves? unsure. They provided sequence numbers showing many 429s then a backlog of retried requests.

kevin-ml: Can we get GPU queue depth and batch-window stats for pods serving rex-3b-quant between 10:00-10:10Z? monitor-bot: collecting metrics for model=rex-3b-quant, timeframe=10:00-10:15Z. ETA ~30s.

dyson-ops: I pulled the trace. Observed that when auth throttles popped, the autosplit/batcher shrank batch windows from 25ms to 3ms due to low observed latency, leading to suboptimal tiny-batches. GPU utilization dipped and per-token overhead dominated so vectors/sec fell.

kevin-ml: That explains tokens/sec staying fine (fast token generation) but vectors/sec dropping (batching inefficiency + overhead). Any evidence of dim mismatch log?

maria-support: The dim warnings line up with a downstream verifier process that runs async and flags messages that got retried mid-flight (partial cache hits). Looks like retried requests cause a mismatch between cached prefix shape vs current request, triggers a soft-fail log but still returns a vector. Could increase CPU overhead.

aj-eng: Action items: 1) Ask customer to replay traffic with reduced client-side retry jitter (simple linear backoff) to see if vectors/sec recovers. 2) Ops: temporarily disable aggressive billing throttle for acme-corp so we can test. 3) Runtime: add a fallback that treats dimension_mismatch warnings as non-blocking and avoids extra CPU pathing for retried requests.

maria-support: I sent ACME an isolated repro script for a 5-min run with no retries + same batch_size. They will run in ~15m.

monitor-bot: results ready for 10:00-10:15Z window: avg_batch_size dropped from 48 -> 7 during throttle spikes; avg_gpu_util 78% -> 24%; vectors/sec per pod 1150 -> 170.

kevin-ml: Confirmed. This is batching/window contraction problem caused by auth/billing retries creating microbursts. Not a model kernel regression. Still want to suppress noisy dim_mismatch logs.

dyson-ops: I lifted the billing throttle for acme-corp for 10m and started a canary with their replay.

maria-support: ACME replayed with retries disabled — vectors/sec recovered to expected levels. Customer very happy. :tada: They say their SDK should be updated to exponential backoff.

aj-eng: PR for runtime tweak to treat dim warnings as non-blocking: https://git.redwood/rex/runtime/pull/456 (adds fast-path for verified retries).

maria-support: Closing loop with customer and noting recommended mitigations: client backoff, avoid synchronizing retries, and we will roll runtime soft-fix.

billing-bot: [automated] throttle restored to previous policy at 10:25Z.

maria-support: Marking this resolved. Summary: throughput regression was operational (auth/billing retry bursts) + small logging-induced CPU path; not a model quant/kernel regression.

kevin-ml: Logging follow-up: suppress `embedding_dim_mismatch` to debug level and add a metric for retried-requests-per-org so we can alert earlier.

lina-frontend: Filing SDK advisory: update retry behavior docs + sample backoff config.

maria-support: Thanks team — will file the ticket and update the support case.
